pr.title: Calculate predecessor count directly
pr.description:
Avoid allocating a vector of small vectors merely to determine how many
predecessors each basic block has.

Additionally use u8 and saturating operations. The pass only needs to
distinguish between [0..1] and [2..].
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: PR #138076 is explicitly a performance optimization, not a semantic bug fix. The frozen analysis and source confirm the only changed behavior is how predecessor counts are computed: old code built exact `usize` counts from `predecessors()` and artificially did `pred_count[START_BLOCK] += 1`; new code scans terminator successors into `u8` counts with `saturating_add`. Both derive counts from the same `Terminator::successors()` edges, including duplicates. The only consumers compare `pred_count[destination] > 1` for blocks targeted by `Call` terminators. For every non-START block the old and new counts are identical, so guard decisions are identical. Saturation at 255 preserves the only relevant categories ([0..1] vs [2..]). For START_BLOCK, the dropped artificial increment can only differ if input MIR has a `Call` whose destination is START_BLOCK; if START_BLOCK has no real predecessors, old=1/new=0 both fail `>1`; if it does have a real backedge, old may add an extra call-guard block on a non-critical edge while new does not, but adding such a guard is semantics-preserving (the added block is an unconditional Goto), and SimplifyCfg is documented to remove it. Thus no concrete source-grounded input makes the optimized pass produce a semantically wrong result; there is no historical incorrect transformation to encode. The PR contains no regression test or bug claim, and manufacturing an unrelated return-value or CFG rewrite would not be evidence for this change.

analysis.originalLogic: The original AddCallGuards implementation built exact per-block predecessor counts by materializing predecessor lists: `body.basic_blocks.predecessors().iter().map(|ps| ps.len()).collect()` into `IndexVec<_, _>`, then performed `pred_count[START_BLOCK] += 1`. This allocated a vector of small vectors and stored full `usize` counts even though the pass only needs to distinguish blocks with at most one predecessor from blocks with two or more.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically pre-optimization transformation is not a semantically wrong guard rewrite; it is an inefficient one. It computes full predecessor lists and exact `usize` lengths, and unconditionally increments `START_BLOCK`. The optimized replacement initializes `IndexVec::from_elem(0u8, &body.basic_blocks)` and scans each block's `data.terminator().successors()`, applying `pred_count[succ].saturating_add(1)`. This is a performance optimization, not a confirmed bug fix: no evidence in the patch shows wrong call guards from the old code.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by the AddCallGuards MIR pass: arbitrary function CFGs with basic blocks, terminators, `START_BLOCK`, call terminators, blocks with zero, one, or many predecessors, loops/self-edges, and possibly duplicate predecessor edges. The relevant count domain is only the categories `[0..1]` and `[2..]`, not exact predecessor counts.
analysis.summary: AddCallGuards replaced allocation of per-block predecessor lists and exact `usize` counts with a direct successor scan into a `u8` `IndexVec` using `saturating_add`, exploiting that the pass only needs to distinguish `[0..1]` from `[2..]`. The dropped synthetic `START_BLOCK` increment is safe under that category-only invariant. This is an optimization, not a confirmed bug fix.
analysis.trigger: Running the AddCallGuards MIR pass, which needs predecessor counts to decide where call guards/critical-edge handling are required.
preconditions: Only the categories [0..1] and [2..] are semantically relevant to AddCallGuards.
Every terminator successor edge counted in the replacement scan must correspond to the predecessor edges the old `predecessors()`-based count represented.
The count type is `u8`, so high-degree blocks must saturate rather than wrap or panic.
`START_BLOCK` may have count 0 instead of the old artificial 1 because both values fall in the same [0..1] category for this pass.
pitfalls: Using ordinary `u8 += 1` instead of `saturating_add` can overflow or panic on CFGs with more than 255 incoming edges; saturation at 255 still preserves the `[2..]` category.
Do not replace category logic with exact-count logic: the optimized count intentionally does not represent exact predecessor counts beyond the saturation/category threshold.
Removing `pred_count[START_BLOCK] += 1` is only safe because the pass distinguishes `[0..1]` from `[2..]`; future logic that needs START_BLOCK to be exactly one or at least one would invalidate this.
The direct successor scan must count successor edges consistently with the previous predecessor-list construction, including any repeated edges, or guard insertion decisions can change.
Avoid reintroducing the allocation of a vector of vectors merely to obtain counts; this was the performance problem being removed.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-focused tests (for example MIR dumps or mir-opt tests) with functions whose CFGs contain blocks having 0, 1, 2, and several predecessors, call terminators at join blocks, self-loops, and duplicate/multiple edges, plus `START_BLOCK`. Compare the call guards/critical-edge splits produced by the original exact-count logic and the optimized category-count logic: the transformed MIR should be identical. Add a high-degree synthetic/constructed CFG above 255 predecessors to exercise `u8` saturation and confirm no overflow/panic while still treating the block as `[2..]`. The supplied patch contains only the `add_call_guards.rs` source hunk and no regression-test changes, so tests must be designed around CFG predecessor categories rather than inferred from updated expectations.
